A simulated EV charge point that speaks **OCPP 1.6J** and **OCPP 2.0.1** over WebSocket, and the pytest suite
that proves it behaves.

### What is in it

- **269 tests across four passes of the suite** — OCPP 1.6 and 2.0.1, each in memory and over a real WebSocket —
  plus 21 browser tests of the visual page. Every test is one plain sentence.
- **The standard is the judge.** Every message in both directions is validated against the JSON schemas
  published with the standard (78 files for 1.6, 128 for 2.0.1), read out of the `ocpp` package rather than
  written here.
- **Somebody else at the other end.** The interoperability suite puts the reference `ocpp` library on one side
  of a real socket and this project on the other, in both directions.
- **41 of 41 planted bugs caught** by `scripts/mutants.py`, with a passing control run.
- **Five visual pages** (EN/RU): the project in two minutes, a live charge point you can operate and sabotage,
  one message taken apart field by field, the last run replayed with its real messages, and the bug hunt.

### What it covers

The OCPP-J envelope and its refusals · a session from cable to invoice · accepted, blocked, expired and unknown
cards · the network going down mid-charge · smart-charging limits and the 6 A floor of IEC 61851-1 · remote
start, stop, reset and connector availability · the pilot states A/B/C/E · random text, oversized and nested
payloads · interoperability both ways.

### Findings

Five, all fixed and pinned by tests — including a 1.6 session that named the wrong transaction after an outage
(wrong invoices), a 2.0.1 status reported twice in a row, and the two versions writing the same meter reading in
shapes each other's schema rejects. [`docs/test-report.md`](https://github.com/NailKarimov/ev-charging-testing/blob/main/docs/test-report.md), section 3.

### Known deviation

Interoperability is proven against the reference `ocpp` library rather than a packaged back office
(CitrineOS, EVerest): the container registry was not reachable from the build environment. That is the first
item for the next version.
